LESSON: GUIDED READING VOCABULARY FLUENCY PHONICS ARTICULATION

Grade: Grade 6
Subject: FRENCH
Strand: Reading 2.7 Reading aloud Pronunciation Rhythm Pacing Phonics By the end of the 
Topic 2.8: Guided reading Vocabulary Fluency Phonics Articulation

SECTION 1: WELCOME

• Today’s class: Guided reading Vocabulary Fluency Phonics Articulation
• How we learn: Teach → Worked example → Try this
• Use point notes. Show working. Then take the quiz.
• Big question: How do you read a word you have not seen before?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

1. read longer words using look-and-say
2. chunk long words into parts
3. build word ladders

SECTION 3: CLASS STUDY (TEACH → EXAMPLE → TRY)

▸ Look-and-say

Teach
• Look at the whole word.
• Listen to the model.
• Say it.
• Cover and write it.

Worked example
• Word: elephant → look → say “elephant” → write it.

Try this
• Practise: giraffe, cucumber, helicopter

▸ Chunking

Teach
• Split a long word into known parts.

Worked example
• football = foot + ball
• classroom = class + room
• sunshine = sun + shine

Try this
• Chunk: handmade, bedroom, toothbrush

▸ Word ladder

Teach
• Change one letter at a time.
• Read every new word.

Worked example
• sun → run → ran
• cat → hat → hot → hop

Try this
• Make a ladder of 4 steps starting from “pen”


SECTION: QUICK EXAMPLES

• elephant (look-and-say)
• football = foot + ball
• sun → run → ran

SECTION: PRACTICE NOW

1. Read 8 long words pointing under each.
2. Chunk 5 compound words.
3. Build one word ladder with 4 steps.

SECTION: WORK TO DO

1. Copy 10 new words. Read them to a parent.
2. Make flashcards for 5 hard words.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How do you read a word you have not seen before?

SECTION: REMEMBER

• Look, say, write.
• Use chunks for long words.
• Practise weekly.

• Next: complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Classroom study notes (Strategy 2)
